_README: Which committed clauses answer 'What should I do next?' for each scheme.
This file holds NO facts. Every entry is the id of a clause already in
data/schemes/<slug>/scheme.md, so whatever a person is shown -- the plain
gloss, the verbatim quote, the page and the official source link -- comes
from the span-validated corpus. tests/api/test_next_steps.py fails if an id
does not exist or has the wrong clause type for its section.
Sections and the clause types they may hold:
benefits      benefit                -- what the person could receive
documents     document               -- what to keep ready
apply         procedure              -- where and how to apply
after         procedure, benefit     -- what happens once enrolled
good_to_know  exclusion, procedure   -- limits worth knowing first
An empty list is an honest gap: the checklist then says the reviewed
official text does not cover it, and points to the official source and
the authority named in the scheme's frontmatter. Do not fill a gap here by
naming a clause that does not actually say it; add the missing clause
through the gated workflow (draft -> import_draft.py -> review.py) and
list it here afterwards. Proposed clauses for the current gaps are in
docs/next-steps-clause-proposals.md.
Choosing which clauses belong to a scheme's applicant route is an
editorial judgement (PMFME's FPO, SHG and branding clauses do not apply
to an individual applicant). Review edits here with the same care as
data/attributes.json.
